seoTitle: Work Hours Calculator - Time Card & Timesheet Tool
metaDescription: Free online Work Hours Calculator. Easily calculate total hours worked in a week, subtracting unpaid lunch breaks. Perfect for timesheets and payroll.
intro: Struggling to calculate exactly how many hours you worked this week? Tracking your daily start times, end times, and unpaid lunch breaks across multiple days can quickly become a tedious and error-prone chore. Our free online Work Hours Calculator simplifies timesheet management by doing all the heavy lifting for you. Just enter your clock-in time, clock-out time, and the duration of your breaks for each day, and the tool will instantly compute your daily totals and your overall weekly hours. Whether you are an hourly employee verifying your paycheck, a freelancer billing a client, or a manager approving timesheets, this tool guarantees absolute accuracy.
whatIs: The Work Hours Calculator is a comprehensive timesheet utility designed to compute exact working durations from standard clock times. Unlike a simple duration calculator that only measures the difference between two points in time, a work hours calculator is specifically tailored for employment scenarios. It natively understands the concept of unpaid breaks (like a 30-minute or 1-hour lunch) and automatically deducts them from the total elapsed time. It supports tracking across a standard 5-day or 7-day workweek, seamlessly handling AM/PM formatting, 24-hour time, and shifts that cross over midnight. It is an indispensable tool for accurate payroll processing and personal time tracking.
howToUse: Enter your unpaid break duration (e.g., 30 minutes).
The tool calculates the exact hours and minutes worked, and the decimal equivalent.
howItWorks: For each day, the calculator requires a start time, an end time, and an optional break duration. The underlying JavaScript engine converts your start and end times into a standard date-time object. It calculates the total elapsed minutes between the two times—intelligently handling scenarios where the end time is on the following day (e.g., a night shift from 10 PM to 6 AM). It then subtracts the unpaid break minutes from that total. This daily net total is converted back into an hours-and-minutes format. Finally, it sums up the net totals from every active day to generate a cumulative weekly total, updating instantly as you type.
workedExample: Imagine tracking your hours for Monday through Wednesday. On Monday, you clock in at 8:30 AM and clock out at 5:00 PM, with a 30-minute unpaid lunch. The tool calculates 8.5 elapsed hours, subtracts 0.5 hours for lunch, yielding 8 hours. On Tuesday, you work a split shift: 9:00 AM to 1:00 PM (4 hours). On Wednesday, you work a night shift: 10:00 PM to 6:00 AM the next day, with no break. The tool recognizes the overnight shift and calculates 8 hours. The calculator instantly sums Monday (8h), Tuesday (4h), and Wednesday (8h) to display a total of 20 hours and 0 minutes for the week.
resultInterpretation: The calculator provides both a daily breakdown and a grand total for the week. The daily totals show exactly how much payable time you accumulated on that specific day after break deductions. The grand total is the number you should use for your timesheet or invoice. The results are typically displayed in both hours-and-minutes format (e.g., 38 hours 30 minutes) and decimal format (e.g., 38.5 hours), as many payroll systems require decimal inputs. If you are calculating overtime, you can easily compare this grand total against your standard weekly threshold (e.g., 40 hours) to see exactly how much overtime pay you are owed.
useCases: Employee Timesheets: Hourly workers verifying their own hours at the end of the week before submitting them to management.
Freelance Billing: Independent contractors tracking exact hours worked on a client project to generate an invoice.
Manager Approvals: Shift supervisors quickly checking if an employee's manual math on a paper timecard is accurate.
tipsAndLimitations: Most payroll systems use decimal hours, not minutes. Remember that 8 hours and 15 minutes is 8.25 hours, not 8.15 hours.
The tool assumes the shift takes place on a single calendar day. Shifts that cross midnight (like 10 PM to 6 AM) require a calculator that understands date wrapping.

faq.question: How do you convert minutes to decimals?
faq.answer: Divide the minutes by 60. For example, 45 minutes divided by 60 equals 0.75. So, 7 hours and 45 minutes is written as 7.75 hours on a timesheet.

faq.question: Do I subtract my lunch break?
faq.answer: In most jurisdictions, yes. If you are entirely relieved of your duties and free to leave the premises during a 30-minute lunch, that time is legally unpaid and should be subtracted from your total hours.

cta: Calculate your weekly work hours now!
disclaimer: This tool strictly calculates elapsed time minus breaks. Consult your local labor laws regarding mandatory paid rest breaks versus unpaid meal periods.
